title: Stephen Miller cracks down on White House cash loophole his own wife used: WSJ
html:
White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, flanked by US Vice President JD Vance, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and US President Donald Trump, speaks during a press conference held by Trump after returning from Asia, in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington, DC, US, November 20, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein

White House chief of staff Stephen Miller is moving to crack down on a lucrative perk that his wife, Katie Miller, once used.

According to a Saturday report by The Wall Street Journal, Miller has told associates that he plans to wind down the use of "special government employees," a designation that allows people to work for an administration while still collecting outside paychecks. Insider sources told The Journal about Miller's plans.

Katie Miller came under fire last year after The Journal revealed that she was working at the White House as a special government employee while also advising private clients. She defended herself by later saying that she had taken leave from her job at a prominent Republican communications firm during her work with the Trump administration. She left the White House in May 2025 and announced she'll halt her podcast after Stephen Miller took over as chief of staff.

Special government employees are allowed to hold onto private salaries and investments while working at the White House, and only a fraction of them must publicly disclose clients or conflicts of interest. Federal rules cap their maximum amount of service at 130 days per year, but the administration can extend that window, per The Journal.

Previous administrations have generally used the special government employee status to bring in subject matter experts for advisory boards or narrow roles, according to The Journal. Under Trump, the status was used to bring on Elon Musk to lead the Department of Government Efficiency, Corey Lewandowski as a top adviser at the Department of Homeland Security and tech entrepreneur David Sacks as Trump's AI and crypto czar, The Journal noted.

A White House official told The Journal that Miller wants to put full-time hires first and rein in what he considers abuse of the designation. Two people familiar with his plans said the White House won't scrap the status altogether but instead rely on special government employees far less.

summary: The White House plans to sharply reduce its use of "special government employees," a designation that lets private-sector workers serve in the administration while keeping their outside salaries and investments, The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday.
